Confirms: desired state is declarative, versioned and immutable, pulled automatically by software agents, and continuously reconciled: agents continuously observe actual state and attempt to apply the desired state.

The organization, the systems and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You run the delivery platform at Marlow Freight, a fictional logistics company. Argo CD reconciles the orders service from a config repository with automated sync and self-heal. Release v2.4 went out 40 minutes ago and the service is degraded.
handover: Automated sync with prune and selfHeal is on for orders.
Nobody was told the release degraded; a customer reported it.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

rollbackPrompt.title: How to roll back
rollbackPrompt.context: v2.3 was healthy; v2.4 is not.

choices.label: git revert the v2.4 commit in the config repo and let Argo CD reconcile orders back to v2.3

effects.log: Argo CD syncs to the reverted commit; orders runs v2.3.

choices.feedback: In GitOps a rollback is a change to desired state: revert the commit and the reconciler does the rest, with history kept.

choices.label: Turn off automated sync and use Argo CD's rollback to the previous sync

effects.log: Auto-sync is off; the app is rolled back.

choices.feedback: It restores service, but Git still says v2.4 and automation is off until someone fixes Git.

choices.label: kubectl set image on the live Deployment to v2.3
choices.feedback: Self-heal sees the drift from Git and puts v2.4 back within minutes.

loopPrompt.title: Nobody saw the degradation
loopPrompt.context: Argo CD showed Degraded for 40 minutes; no one was told.

choices.label: Subscribe the team channel to Argo CD notifications for on-health-degraded and on-sync-failed, and link the alert to the app's dashboard

effects.log: Degraded and failed syncs now reach the team.

choices.feedback: Observed state has to reach operators; reconciler notifications close the loop.

choices.label: Ask the release engineer to watch the Argo CD UI after each release
choices.feedback: Better than nothing, but only while someone is looking.

choices.label: Customize orders' health check to always report Healthy so the dashboard stays green
choices.feedback: A green dashboard that cannot turn red hides the next failure.

continuousPrompt.title: A team calls its pipeline GitOps
continuousPrompt.context: The billing team's CI runs kubectl apply once after each build and calls it GitOps.

choices.label: Bring billing under Argo CD: CI only commits the new version to the config repo, and the reconciler keeps comparing and applying desired state
choices.feedback: Continuous means an agent keeps reconciling, not a one-time apply after each build.

choices.label: Keep CI's apply but run it every hour too

effects.log: An hourly apply job is added.

choices.feedback: Drift is fixed hourly at best, and CI still holds cluster credentials.

choices.label: Accept it as GitOps and remove Argo CD from billing to save resources

effects.log: Billing deploys by CI apply only.

choices.feedback: Nothing watches the live state; a hand edit stays until the next build.

scoring.modelReasoning: In GitOps, rollback is a change to desired state: revert the commit and the reconciler applies it, with history kept. Hand edits fight self-heal, and Argo CD will not roll back an app under automated sync. Observed state informs operators only if it reaches them, so notify on degraded health and failed syncs. Continuous means an agent keeps reconciling; a one-time CI apply is not GitOps.
